purpose: Sources actually consulted for the antiquity-first observatory, scale audit and rendering review; exact access scope is explicit.

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.title: Parts of Animals, Book I, chapter 1
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text passage: method, common processes, phenomena, causes, and hypothetical necessity.
sources.usable_claim: The passage distinguishes shared processes from differences among organisms and asks how inquiry should move from phenomena to causes.
sources.limits: Its prioritization of final causes is an ancient philosophical position, not an implemented ecological force or evidence that nature guarantees outcomes.

sources.author: Theophrastus
sources.title: Enquiry into Plants, volume II, VII.5 and VIII.10–11
sources.period: Late fourth to early third century BCE
sources.access_scope: Scan OCR: printed pages 95–97 and 203–209, with section headers and translation title page.
sources.usable_claim: Distinguishes seed keeping from germination, moisture and locality effects, and variation among plants; explicitly reports exceptions to usual longevity.
sources.limits: OCR and ancient plant identification introduce uncertainty. Spontaneous-generation explanations and exceptional longevity reports are not physical parameters. No universal four-year seed lifetime is inferred.

sources.author: Hippocratic corpus
sources.title: On Airs, Waters, and Places, part 1
sources.period: Late fifth or early fourth century BCE
sources.access_scope: Full opening passage on investigating seasons, winds, waters, aspect, ground, and local habits.
sources.usable_claim: Offers a historically grounded question set for observing environmental variation before explaining local health.
sources.limits: This methodological passage does not validate humoral medicine or climatic explanations of group character. Only part 1 is used.

sources.author: Xenophon
sources.title: Oeconomicus (The Economist), chapters IX and XVI
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text chapters on household stores, monthly/yearly provision, observation of crops, and learning land suitability.
sources.usable_claim: Distinguishes storage conditions and timescales; reasons from visible land and neighboring cultivation.
sources.limits: A literary dialogue from an elite agrarian context is not an ethnographic census or proof of general agricultural effectiveness. Its gender and slavery assumptions are not simulation rules.

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.title: Politics, Book I, parts VIII–IX
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text passages on subsistence, acquisition, the shoe's uses, exchange, coin, and the Midas example.
sources.usable_claim: Distinguishes useful provision from exchange value and monetary accumulation.
sources.limits: The naturalness of slavery, human-centered teleology, and a universal barter-to-money history are not accepted as physical or historical laws.

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.title: Nicomachean Ethics, Book I, chapters 1–4
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text opening chapters on different ends, appropriate precision, and disagreement about living well.
sources.usable_claim: Provides questions about the ends of activities and the precision warranted by different kinds of inquiry.
sources.limits: Aristotle argues for an ordering of goods; the text is not evidence that he endorsed the simulation's plural outcome vector or that one ethical hierarchy must be encoded.

sources.author: Polybius
sources.title: Histories, Book VI, chapters 9 and 11–18
sources.translation: W. R. Paton; public Loeb text hosted by LacusCurtius
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text account of Roman offices, supply and financial dependence, treaty ratification, and the constitutional-cycle claim.
sources.usable_claim: Describes authority through mutually dependent decisions and supplies rather than an office name alone.
sources.limits: The account favors a mixed constitution. Its claim of an inevitable cycle and unmatched institutional success is not a transition timer or universal validation.

sources.author: Traditionally attributed to Kautilya
sources.title: Arthashastra, Book II, chapter XV
sources.period: Ancient South Asian statecraft; composite text with debated date and authorship
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text chapter, The Superintendent of Storehouse: inflows, loans, processing, old-stock replacement, and reserves.
sources.usable_claim: Distinguishes kinds of inventory flow and calls for tracking changes in material through processing.
sources.limits: Prescriptions are not measured practice. Do not import the half-stock rule, caste/sex ration hierarchy, or volume-expansion ratios as universal laws; added water and mass must be accounted for.

sources.author: Ibn Khaldun
sources.title: Muqaddimah, first prefatory discussion
sources.period: Fourteenth century CE; first composed in 1377
sources.translation: English online excerpt hosted by MuslimPhilosophy
sources.access_scope: Full online prefatory discussion of social cooperation, food preparation, crafts, defense, and restraining authority.
sources.usable_claim: Presents cooperation as a combination of complementary activities and tools; distinguishes an argument for authority from a claimed logical necessity for prophecy.
sources.limits: Universal claims about solitary subsistence, aggression, royal authority, and divine purpose are arguments in context, not model laws. The accessed page does not supply a complete critical edition.

sources.author: IPCC
sources.title: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, volume 4, chapter 4: Forest Land
sources.access_scope: Tables 4.3, 4.7, and 4.9, printed pages 4.48, 4.53–4.54, and 4.57–4.58; biomass table 4.7 visually checked after rendering.
sources.usable_claim: Supplies distinct dry-matter stock and annual net aboveground growth defaults, by ecological zone and age class, with ranges.
sources.limits: These are inventory defaults, not a local calibration. Net aboveground growth is not edible yield or total NPP. The underlying references cited in the tables were not independently read.

sources.author: Pontzer, Raichlen, Wood, Mabulla, Racette, and Marlowe
sources.title: Hunter-Gatherer Energetics and Human Obesity
sources.access_scope: Full-text abstract, methods, results, and selected discussion; 30-adult Hadza study with an 11-day expenditure measurement period.
sources.usable_claim: Reports mean daily walking distances of 5.8 ± 1.7 km for women and 11.4 ± 2.1 km for men; uses GPS and doubly labeled water methods.
sources.limits: Daily path length is not radial range or sustainable yield. One population and season do not calibrate every community, sex role, climate, or carrying capacity.

sources.author: FAO; J. Proctor, editor
sources.title: Grain Storage Techniques: Evolution and Trends in Developing Countries, chapter 2, Biodeterioration
sources.access_scope: Full biodeterioration section and book title/contents.
sources.usable_claim: Explains interacting moisture, temperature, oxygen, physical damage, and organisms; contrasts 15%-moisture maize at 15°C and 30°C.
sources.limits: No universal food-loss rate or Q10=2 calibration follows. It concerns grain, and some moulds can grow below freezing. Studies cited by the chapter were not independently read.

sources.author: Hill et al.
sources.title: Co-residence patterns in hunter-gatherer societies show unique human social structure
sources.access_scope: Europe PMC abstract and bibliographic record, PMID 21393537; full article not read.
sources.usable_claim: Abstract reports 5,067 individuals in 32 societies, mean experienced band size 28.2 adults, dispersal by either sex, and many genetically unrelated coresidents.
sources.limits: A residential band is not an isolated breeding population. The abstract supplies no minimum viable founder count, fertility calibration, or universal kinship rule.

sources.author: D. Lawrence Venable
sources.title: Bet hedging in a guild of desert annuals
sources.access_scope: Europe PMC abstract and bibliographic record, PMID 17536393; full article not read.
sources.usable_claim: Abstract reports a 22-year dataset for ten desert annual species and an association of higher variation in reproductive success with lower average germination fractions.
sources.limits: This does not set a universal dormancy fraction, prove intent or foresight in plants, or calibrate temperate perennial reserves.

sources.author: Morelli et al.
sources.title: Managing Climate Change Refugia for Climate Adaptation
sources.access_scope: Full-text sections on vulnerability, refugium identification/validation, connectivity, monitoring, and limits.
sources.usable_claim: Refugial effectiveness depends on buffering processes, the focal species/resource, connectivity, scale, and duration; independent validation is needed.
sources.limits: A refugium is not an invulnerable tile or an automatic recolonization source. Management recommendations and empirical examples are distinct.

sources.author: Vaesen, Collard, Cosgrove, and Roebroeks
sources.title: Population size does not explain past changes in cultural complexity
sources.access_scope: Europe PMC abstract and bibliographic record, PMID 27044082; available full article not read in this batch.
sources.usable_claim: The abstract presents a critique of demographic explanations of archaeological cultural complexity and their model assumptions.
sources.limits: This is a critical position, not proof that demography never matters. Competing studies require direct examination before a calibrated cultural model is proposed.

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.title: On the Heavens, Book II, chapter 14
sources.access_scope: Selected closing full-text passages on Earth's shape, lunar-eclipse shadows, changing visible stars, and the reported circumference; translation title and surrounding physical argument.
sources.usable_claim: Connects changes in observations at different places and a curved eclipse shadow with the question of a finite spherical Earth.
sources.limits: Geocentric cosmology, natural-place arguments, an eternal world, the elephant argument, and the quoted 400,000 stades are not adopted as physical law or numerical calibration. No unqualified conversion of the ancient stade is made.

sources.author: Vitruvius
sources.title: The Ten Books on Architecture, Book III, chapter IV, sections 1–2
sources.access_scope: Title/translation page and selected full-text passage on temple foundations, load-bearing substructures, solid ground, and piles in loose or marshy ground; adjacent sections inspected for context.
sources.usable_claim: Distinguishes the load, the supporting ground, and foundations under different ground conditions; below-ground support is a material relationship.
sources.limits: A Roman architectural prescription is not measured bearing strength. Temple proportions, named wood treatments, and ritual step preferences are not universal engineering rules. No ancient length unit is silently mapped to a modern metre.

sources.author: Georgius Agricola
sources.title: De Re Metallica, Book V
sources.translation: Herbert Clark Hoover and Lou Henry Hoover, 1912; 1950 unaltered reprint
sources.access_scope: Translation/title pages; selected authorial passages on shafts, tunnels, excavated materials, uncertain ore indications, drainage, circulation of air, and support in hard versus weak rock. Translator footnotes distinguished from the main text.
sources.usable_claim: Describes underground work as a connected system of access, haulage, waste, water, air, power, and supports; ore indications can disappoint and require investigation.
sources.limits: Not a modern mine-design manual or calibrated constitutive law. The explanations of vapours, fixed seasonal air patterns, empirical dimensions, and claims of perfect safety are not adopted. Fathoms and feet are not converted without a historical-unit study.

sources.author: NASA Science
sources.title: Earth Facts
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text sections: Size and Distance, Orbit and Rotation, Moons, Structure, and Surface; quick-fact labels checked.
sources.usable_claim: Checks the orders of magnitude of Earth–Sun and Earth–Moon distances, planetary size, annual/day cycles, and kilometre-scale interior layers.
sources.limits: Public educational summary, not a primary measurement dataset. Rounded sidereal-day and equatorial-diameter values differ in meaning from the model's 24-hour solar day and spherical mean radius. Exact code constants are reported as assumptions; the page's simplified mantle wording is not used as a material model.

sources.author: U.S. Geological Survey
sources.title: Inside the Earth, This Dynamic Earth
sources.access_scope: Full main page and page metadata; diagram captions read, underlying seismic studies not consulted.
sources.usable_claim: Gives approximate oceanic and continental crust thicknesses, a roughly 2,900 km mantle, a liquid outer core and solid inner core; describes mantle rock as semi-solid with slow flow under heat and pressure.
sources.limits: A broad educational synthesis, not local geological stratigraphy, ore abundance, soil bulk density, or a depth profile for Praxans. Approximate core dimensions differ slightly from newer summaries and are used only for scale.

sources.author: NASA Science
sources.title: Sun Facts
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text overview, Size and Distance, photosphere/core temperature descriptions, and quick-fact labels.
sources.usable_claim: Checks a solar radius near 700,000 km, Sun–Earth distance near 150 million km, and the distinction between photosphere and core temperatures.
sources.limits: An educational order-of-magnitude check, not exact calibration of luminosity, gravitational constants, internal stellar structure, or the simulation's radiation solver.

sources.author: MDN contributors
sources.title: Optimizing canvas
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text sections on caching repeated primitives, static/dynamic canvas layers, scaling, pixel ratio, state changes and animation scheduling.
sources.usable_claim: Repeated drawing can be cached; work with different update rates can be separated; rendering cost and quality depend on scaling and backing pixels.
sources.limits: Platform guidance, not a benchmark of Praxans or every browser. Recommendations such as integer pixel snapping and alpha settings must be checked for the actual projection and context.

sources.author: MDN contributors
sources.title: WebGL best practices
sources.access_scope: Selected full-text sections on device limits, static buffers, resource deletion, blocking API calls, per-pixel VRAM budgets, smaller backing buffers, draw batching, mipmaps and high-DPI rendering.
sources.usable_claim: Portable applications need explicit resource budgets, batching and bounded drawing-buffer sizes; WebGL offers no portable query of all available VRAM.
sources.limits: Guidance is hardware- and workload-dependent. The numerical budgets proposed in this research remain assumptions until measured on target PCs; CPU submission timings are not GPU completion times.

sources.author: MDN contributors
sources.title: Window: requestAnimationFrame() method
sources.access_scope: Full introductory timing, refresh-rate, background-tab and timestamp guidance; selected example explanation of 16.67 ms at 60 Hz.
sources.usable_claim: Animation callbacks follow display refresh rather than a guaranteed fixed rate; timestamps support elapsed-time animation, and most browsers pause callbacks in background tabs.
sources.limits: A 16.67 ms frame interval is arithmetic for 60 Hz, not a promise that an application may spend that entire interval in JavaScript. Hidden DOM panels are not necessarily background tabs.

sources.author: MDN contributors
sources.title: OffscreenCanvas
sources.access_scope: Full introduction and selected transferable-object, worker and ImageBitmap ownership examples.
sources.usable_claim: Some canvas processing can run in a worker, with explicit ownership transfer rather than repeated copies of frame data.
sources.limits: Worker availability and particular rendering contexts still require feature checks. Moving work does not eliminate its CPU, memory, GPU or scheduling cost.

sources.author: MDN contributors
sources.title: PerformanceLongTaskTiming
sources.access_scope: Full introductory definition, main-thread effects, availability warning and PerformanceObserver example.
sources.usable_claim: The interface describes uninterrupted main-thread tasks lasting at least 50 ms; they can delay input and rendering.
sources.limits: The API is not supported in all widely used browsers. Fifty milliseconds is an API threshold, not an acceptable universal latency budget; use fallback frame/input timing where unavailable.
